questions.q: The audit's central control reliance:
o: Substantive-only — IT is not our field
ITGC over access and change: the automated three-way match inherits its credibility from them
Rely on the count of orders
Vendor warranty on the software
questions.why: Fully automated, no manual paper trail: substantive-alone is not sufficient at the assertion level (SA 330's trigger), so controls testing is MANDATORY — and it's the ITGC layer (access + change) that the application controls rest on.

questions.topic: The controls walk — ITGC and revenue
questions.q: Developer with production access breaks:
o: Logical access and change management — ITGC core — reliance collapses for every automated control
Just the payroll cycle
Nothing — the developer is trusted
Segregation in purchasing
questions.why: Permanent privileged access defeats the change-control premise: code can reach production without the controls; the knock-on: automated controls' operating effectiveness can't be presumed ⇒ substantive escalation or remediation testing over the whole year (the 'who changed what' query is the auditor's tool here).

questions.q: The data extract completeness risk:
o: Accept — the system exports everything
The auditor must establish the population's integrity (reconcile extract record counts/totals to the DB, test date-sequence and deletion logic) before any full-population analytics mean anything
Rely on management's certificate of the CSV
Sample 100 rows

questions.topic: The controls walk — ITGC and revenue
questions.q: For 9M orders, the auditor's best revenue evidence:
o: Confirm 500 random orders
Full-population analytics on the extract (price×qty×tax vs billed) + test the interface totals (order system ↔ invoicing ↔ bank collections) and exception drill-downs
Rely on the VAT return
Cut-off test 5 invoices
questions.why: At this volume, sampling cannot give coverage; the efficient path is analytics over the whole population with the interface reconciliation to plug the completeness hole — exceptions are then tested individually.

A description of reliance on controls the auditor must evaluate and test — plus the audit-trail/compliance dimension where applicable for this class of entity

questions.q: Inappropriate as a materiality benchmark for a profit-oriented manufacturing company's financial statements:
o: Profit before tax
Total revenue
Gross bank balance held as fixed deposit
Total assets
questions.why: Benchmarks are what users focus on (PBT, revenue, net assets); a single fixed-deposit balance is not a users' focus — the third option is the odd one out even though it is 'large'.

questions.q: Performance materiality is set below overall materiality primarily to:
o: Reduce audit hours to the client's budget
Reduce the aggregate probability that uncorrected + undetected misstatements exceed overall materiality
Satisfy the regulator mechanically
Replace the need for the clearly-trivial threshold
questions.why: PM addresses the gap between what we find and what we miss: a lower threshold on scope so that the sum of uncorrected and undetected misstatements has a LOW probability of exceeding overall materiality — hence the usual 5–25% haircut range (commonly 50–75% of OM).
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — PM = headroom for the misstatements you did not catch Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Budget the audit for the errors you'll never see.

questions.q: If during fieldwork actual results reveal lower-than-expected profit, materiality:
o: Cannot be revised once set
Is revised if information would have caused a different initial amount — and PM and scope are re-aligned
Doubles automatically
Is set by the audit committee
questions.why: Reconsider when information at planning would have produced a different figure; revising materiality DOWNWARD raises the question whether planned procedures suffice — and whether the previously 'clearly trivial' basket now matters.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — materiality is an estimate that owes the facts an apology AI prediction, not a certainty.

questions.q: A misstatement arising from management's unreasonable accounting estimate, without evidence of intent, is best dealt with as:
o: An error to be corrected; the judgment difference is evaluated for materiality
Automatic fraud
Ignored as subjective
A scope limitation
questions.why: Estimates split difference-OF-view from errors; both accumulate as misstatements for evaluation (SA 450) — fraud classification needs intent/bias indications, which SA 540 pushes the auditor to look for but not presume.

questions.q: Which is NOT a component of internal control as used in audit risk assessment?
o: Control environment
Entity's risk assessment process
Marketing channel strategy
Monitoring of controls
questions.why: The five: control environment; management's risk assessment process; the information system (including relevant business processes); control activities; monitoring — marketing strategy is business, not IC.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — five are memorised by name; the sixth is always business strategy AI prediction, not a certainty.

questions.q: Which statement about the risk of material misstatement (RoMM) is correct?
o: RoMM is created by the auditor's procedures
RoMM exists independently of the audit; detection risk is the auditor's dial
Both are fixed by law
Sampling error is control risk
questions.why: RoMM = inherent × control risk — the entity's condition, assessed not changed; the auditor controls only detection risk by adjusting procedures — the model AR = IR×CR×DR puts the 'D' in the auditor's hands.

questions.q: A significant risk in an audit context typically involves:
o: Routine, predictable transactions
Fraud susceptibility, high estimation uncertainty, or complex/non-routine transactions
Any account above materiality
Departments with high staff turnover
questions.why: Significant risks are identified after inherent risk (before considering controls), marked by susceptibility to material misstatement — fraud, management bias zones (estimates), complex transactions, transactions with significant related-party content.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).

questions.q: Tests of controls are REQUIRED when:
o: The auditor expects low control risk
The auditor intends to rely on controls OR substantive procedures alone cannot provide sufficient appropriate evidence at the assertion level
The client requests it
Materiality is low
questions.why: SA 330: TOC are mandatory (i) where substantive-only is not sufficient (e.g. highly automated processing without audit trails), and (ii) when the risk assessment is predicated on reliance on the operating effectiveness of controls.

questions.q: Because of the risk of management override of controls, the auditor must:
o: Rely on controls that passed last year
Assume it as a significant risk and respond (journal entry testing, reviewing estimates for bias, evaluating business rationale of significant unusual transactions)
Test it only if fraud is alleged
Outsource it to internal audit
questions.why: SA 240 deems management override a fraud risk present in EVERY audit, with mandatory responses — testing journal entries and adjustments for appropriateness, reviewing significant estimates for bias, and evaluating unusual transactions' business rationale.

questions.q: The clearly-trivial threshold exists so that:
o: Misstatements can be ignored
The auditor need not accumulate obviously trivial items — but patterns and bias still count
Management can avoid correcting big items
The auditor can skip testing altogether
questions.why: The CTT is an accumulation filter, not a permission slip: individually trivial items in a biased pattern still aggregate in judgment.

questions.q: Planning materiality is set at 8% of PBT Rs 1,090 lakh; PM is taken at 75% of it and the clearly-trivial threshold at 5% of overall materiality. Compute the three amounts:
o: OM Rs 87 lakh; PM Rs 65 lakh (75%); trivial Rs 4.4 lakh
OM Rs 87 lakh; PM Rs 87 lakh (same)
OM Rs 174 lakh; PM Rs 65 lakh
OM Rs 87 lakh; PM Rs 109 lakh (PM above OM)
questions.why: OM = 1090 × 8% = 87; PM = ×75% = 65; trivial = 5% × OM = 4.4 lakh. PM below OM (headroom for undetected error); trivial far below OM (what need not accumulate).
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the ladder is the arithmetic of every audit file Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: PM is a percentage haircut on overall materiality (typically 50–75%); the clearly-trivial threshold is a fraction (e.g. 5%) of OM.
